description: Fork of exp615 (tiny LUT-LM, hybrid_smooth n_alt=1 SoTA = 1.5845). SINGLE change: hybrid_smooth_n_alt=-1 (= NAP per module → full Hamming-1 ball forward) AND hybrid_smooth_autograd=true (plain autograd backward, fully self-consistent gradients via chain rule through forward). NO soft K-row surrogate for input grad — input gradient flows ONLY through the (NAP+1) ball rows in the forward. Tests user hypothesis: at tiny scale where memory fits, does autograd-through-(NAP+1)-row forward + restricted backward beat the 2-row + soft-K-row-surrogate (exp615) approach? Forward: (NAP+1)-way softmax over Hamming-1 ball, computed via gather. Backward via autograd: weight grad scatters at (NAP+1) rows (chain rule of forward), input grad propagates through abs_p → softmax → probs chain. Same backbone as exp365/exp386/exp615.
